## Original request (top authority)

# Tabula: seven more commands

This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
`head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.

How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

The original request outranks the PRD, which outranks the issue. Where they conflict, follow the original request and say so in the PR.

OUTPUT STYLE — caveman, rules inlined here. For your own output and agent-to-agent comments:
handoffs, review findings, checkpoint notes — no human reads them live. Terse: drop articles, filler, pleasantries;
fragments are fine; short synonyms; arrows for causality (X -> Y); technical terms stay exact.
Human-facing artifacts stay plain prose, never caveman: PRD and issue bodies, PR titles and descriptions,
docs, README, CHANGELOG, commit messages. Exact strings are never compressed: code, commands, errors,
file paths, test names, label names, issue and PR refs, `<!-- harness-… -->` marker lines, the promise.

SHARED HOST — stop a background job only by the PID you started (`$!`, or a PID file you wrote) —
never `pkill -f`, `killall`, or `ps … | grep … | kill` by pattern. This host runs many lanes; a
pattern kill can hit theirs.
A PID read from a file or variable must be checked as non-empty, all digits and greater than 1
before it reaches `kill` or `pgrep -P`. Never write `pgrep -P ${p:-0}`: a missing or empty pidfile
becomes PID 0, `pgrep -P 0` lists PID 1's children, and killing them takes down `systemd --user` and
every fleet on the host. Never signal PID 0, PID 1 or a negative PID.
LONG WAITS (#1042, #1066) — never wait inside your session; the engine waits for you. Your prompt cache lives 5 minutes: a foreground `sleep` loop that wakes after 9-10 minutes rewrites your whole context as a cache write (150K-300K tokens, about $1 per wake on Sonnet, against about $0.08 for a cache read), and that pattern was 72% of three days' spend. A job that may run longer than about 4 minutes (a suite, a gate, a bench batch, a Windows-host run, a build): start it with `harness-wait run --deadline-s <most seconds it may take> --log <logfile> -- <command…>`, then END YOUR TURN at once: one short reply naming what you wait for (no promise, no more tool calls). `harness-wait run` starts the command detached, keeps its output in the log and its exit code in `<logfile>.rc`, and writes your wait spec; the engine checks it for you at no model cost and resumes this session ONCE, when the job exits or the deadline passes, with `wait done: <condition>, rc=<n>, log tail: …`. Judge the result from that message and read the log for more; never loop on it. Other conditions: `harness-wait set --deadline-s <s> --pid <pid>` (a process exits), `--path <file>` (a file appears), `--regex <re> --log <file>` (a line appears in a log from now on). Not allowed, whatever the Bash timeout: `for i in $(seq 1 58); do …; sleep 10; done`, `timeout 585 bash -c "until …"`, `end=$((SECONDS+570)); while …`, or a Bash `run_in_background` you then keep polling. A wait on another lane (a lock queue, a merge, a PR) is not a job you can run: park the lane where a park exists (a lock queue, #1034) instead of polling. A usage limit needs nothing from you: the engine parks the lane and resumes it once the limit has cleared. If you park yourself on a limit or a reset time (`harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`), omit `--deadline-s`: the deadline resumes you too, and `waitlib` refuses one that ends before `--until` (#1100). A wait that ends HOURS from now (more than 2 hours: a bench or budget block waiting for a usage window to reset, `harness-wait set --limit --until <epoch>`, or `--path <file> --deadline-s <s>`) PARKS you (#1154): commit and push first, then run it; it posts your handoff, swaps `agent-working` for the `waiting-quota` label and ends your session, so your pool slot goes to the next ready issue, and the engine re-dispatches the issue as a resume once the wait is over — do nothing more after it prints `PARKED`. A refusal (unpushed work) leaves your session as it was; `--resume inject` keeps your slot, and is for waits you really must hold. Never sit on a pool slot for hours. Polling you cannot avoid: one short check per wake, each wake under 270 seconds so the cache stays warm. Never a blocking loop. SUB-AGENTS (#1249) — your own sub-agents are not jobs you can wait on, and each one's notification is a wake after the 5-minute cache expired (140K-350K tokens of cache write each; four bangwa lanes were parked for it). Sub-agents always run in the background here. Start every sub-agent of one fan-out in ONE message, so they start together and tend to finish together. Every sub-agent brief tells it to run every command in the foreground: no `run_in_background`, `Monitor` or `harness-wait run` inside a sub-agent, and never end its turn before its final report. Each sub-agent then notifies you exactly once; one that backgrounds its work and ends its turn sends an interim "completed" you pay a wake for, and a second when it really finishes. When a sub-agent's notification arrives while other sub-agents are still running, make no tool calls: write one short line and end your turn (no re-reading files, no `git status`, no check on the others). Never poll a sub-agent (`TaskOutput`, reading its output file, or `sleep`). The engine sets a context budget (`HARNESS_LANE_CONTEXT_MAX`, default 200k) and Claude Code compacts a lane and each of its sub-agents when it reaches it; stay well under it yourself. A sub-agent is ONE bounded task: its brief names the files it reads and edits, the tests it runs and the checkboxes it owns, and nothing more. It never reads the whole repo (no tree-wide `git grep`, `find` or `cat` sweeps, no files outside its brief) and never pastes a whole file, diff or test log into its context: it reads the lines it needs, tails and greps logs. It hands back a SUMMARY of at most 30 lines (what changed, the test result, any defect it did not fix), never file contents. A merge or conflict-resolution sub-agent resolves ONLY the files it is given, one conflicted file or a few that depend on each other, reading those files, their conflict markers and the commit messages of the two sides, and nothing else; the rest of the merge stays with its parent. Work that runs on (about 100 calls) goes to a FRESH sub-agent with a new brief, never to a longer-running one; you keep the summaries, not their transcripts.

# Tabula: seven more commands

This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
`head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.

How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
error. At least one KEY is needed.

## filter

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
table with no row left still prints its header.

## group

`tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
`mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
`2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
usage error.

## join

`tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
`max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

## Order of work

File this as seven issues, one per command, so each can be built, tested and merged on its own. The seven commands do
not depend on each other, but they share the module, the option reading, the number helpers, `docs/commands.md` and the
README list, so expect to touch the same lines as the others. Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them:
do not add a second way to do something it already does.

PRD: tabula — seven more commands (sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats) [{'id': 'LA_kwDOVyybsc8AAAADDn47Mg', 'name': 'prd', 'description': 'PRD tracking issue', 'color': '5319e7'}]
## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python 3.9+, standard library only) has four commands (`show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`) in `tabula/engine.py`. The user wants seven more table commands — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — plus two new options, `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`. Everything that works today has to keep working: the four commands, their output, their exit statuses, `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command, and `import tabula`.

## Solution

Each command is a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function in `tabula/engine.py` that returns a `Table`, with one entry in `COMMANDS`. Each also gets its own test file `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after the four existing sections and written like them) and a line in the README command list.

Before anything is added, the conventions the module already has become one shared helper each (see Implementation Decisions). Every new command uses those helpers. None of them adds a second way to do the same thing.

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I can `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers and get a stable multi-key sort.
2. As a CSV user, I can `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` with `== != >= <= > < ~` and get only the rows where every condition holds.
3. As a CSV user, I can `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`.
4. As a CSV user, I can `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` with `--kind inner|left`.
5. As a CSV user, I can `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to sum VALUE into a cross table.
6. As a CSV user, I can `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` with `--keep first|last`.
7. As a CSV user, I can `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median for each column.
8. As a user of the four existing commands, I see no change in their output or exit statuses.

## Implementation Decisions

General rules, from the brief, for every command:
- `--format text|csv|json` (text by default) prints the result table.
- A mistake in a file or in the request prints `tabula: <message>` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 1 (`TabulaError`).
- A command line that is not shaped right exits 2 (`UsageError`): a missing or extra argument, an unknown option, a bad option value, a condition with no operator.
- A column named in a request that the file lacks exits 1, and the message names the column (reuse `Table.index`).
- "row N" counts the file's data rows from 1, header not counted, in file order (never sorted order).
- A **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts. All arithmetic is `Decimal`, never float.
- **Shape checks come before the file is read.** Usage errors (exit 2) are raised before `load`, as `head` does today. Column-existence and cell mistakes (exit 1) come after.

### Shared groundwork: done in issue 1 (`sort`), reused by the other six

"Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them: do not add a second way to do something it already does."
1. **Option reading.** Replace the hard-coded `--format` branch in `parse_args` with one table of choice options, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": (FORMATS, "text"), "kind": (("inner", "left"), "inner"), "keep": (("first", "last"), "first")}`, read by one loop that handles both `--opt value` and `--opt=value`. Defaults go into `opts`, so `opts["kind"]` and `opts["keep"]` always exist. Any command line accepts all three options, before or after the command. A bad value is a UsageError, as `--format` is today. The existing `--format` messages stay word for word (`--format needs a value`, `--format must be one of text, csv, json, got 'x'`). Update the usage line in `usage_text()` and the intro of `docs/commands.md` to mention `--kind` and `--keep`.
2. **Argument counts.** Extend `_need_args` so it can also check "at least N" (e.g. `_need_args(args, 2, "sort FILE KEY...", at_least=True)`), and make `cmd_apply` use it, with an unchanged message. Every new command checks its count with `_need_args`.
3. **Row/cell errors.** `cmd_apply` already wraps a cell mistake as `"%s: row %d: %s"`. Make that one helper. On top of it, add a cell-number helper built on `_need_number`/`to_decimal` that raises exactly `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number`; `%r` is used for both the column and the value, as `_need_number` does. `sort :num`, `group`, `pivot` and `stats` all use this helper. `apply`'s output is unchanged.
4. **Number printing.** Plain numbers (sum/min/max/pivot cells) use the existing `fmt_decimal`, which gives no exponent, no `+` and no negative zero, and keeps `10.50` as `10.50`. Add one helper for "rounded half up to two decimals, always two" (`Decimal("0.01")`, `ROUND_HALF_UP`, then `fmt_decimal`). `group mean`, `stats mean` and `stats median` all use it. A negative zero such as `-0.001` prints `0.00`.
5. **Value comparison.** Add one helper for "compare as numbers when both are numbers, else as text by code point", used by `filter`. `sort :num` uses the cell-number helper; plain `sort` compares text.
6. **Tests.** Move the `run_cli` helper from `tests/test_engine.py` into a shared test-support module (e.g. `tests/support.py`). `test_engine.py` and every new `tests/test_NAME.py` import it from there. Do not copy it.
7. **README.** Turn the README's inline "Commands today: …" sentence into a bulleted command list, one line per command (the four existing ones first). Each command issue then adds its own line in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats.

### Per-command decisions (brief text plus the gaps the brief left open)

**sort** `sort FILE KEY...` (at least one KEY; usage `sort FILE KEY...`)
- A KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column; each further part must be `num` or `desc`, in either order. A modifier given twice, an unknown modifier, or an empty column part is a usage error.
- Text compares by code point (`B` < `a`). `:num` compares Decimals, and a non-number cell (an empty one included) gives the cell-number error. `:desc` puts the largest first.
- The sort is stable on every key: rows tied on all keys keep file order, also with `:desc`. Use successive stable `sorted` passes from the last key to the first, with `reverse=` for desc. Python's `reverse=True` keeps stability.

**filter** `filter FILE CONDITION...` (at least one)
- Operators: `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`. The operator is the one that starts earliest in the argument; where two start at the same place, the longer one wins. The column is the text before it and VALUE the text after it (VALUE may be empty).
- No operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. An unknown column is exit 1.
- For every operator but `~`: if the cell and VALUE are both numbers (`to_decimal`), they are compared as Decimals (`10` > `9`, `1.0` == `1`); otherwise as text by code point.
- `~`: VALUE is contained in the cell, ignoring case, via `.lower()` on both, as `t_icontains` does.
- Rows stay in file order. With no rows left, the header still prints.

**group** `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (at least one AGGREGATE)
- An AGGREGATE is `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C` or `mean:C`. Anything else (including `count:x`, `sum:` and an unknown name) is a usage error, and so is the same aggregate twice.
- The output columns are BY, then one per aggregate named with `:` replaced by `_`. If that gives the same column name twice (e.g. BY is `count`), it is a mistake (exit 1) naming the column.
- One row per distinct BY value, in order of first appearance. `count` is the number of rows in the group.
- sum/min/max print with `fmt_decimal` (min/max print the Decimal of the winning cell; among equal values, the first in file order wins). `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, printed with the 2-decimal helper. Any non-number cell (an empty one included) in an aggregated column gives the cell-number error.

**join** `join LEFT RIGHT KEY` (exactly three)
- KEY must be in both files (exit 1 otherwise, naming the file and the column).
- The result columns are the LEFT columns, then the RIGHT columns except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` appended. If that still leaves a duplicate name, it is a mistake (exit 1).
- A match is exact text equality. `--kind inner` (the default) gives, for each LEFT row in order, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. `--kind left` also gives an unmatched LEFT row once, with `""` in the RIGHT columns.

**pivot** `pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` (exactly four)
- ROW == COLUMN is a usage error. VALUE may be the same column as ROW or COLUMN.
- The result columns are ROW, then each distinct COLUMN value in order of first appearance. There is one row per distinct ROW value in order of first appearance.
- A cell is the exact sum of VALUE (printed with `fmt_decimal`); a pair that never occurs is `0`.
- Mistakes are checked row by row in file order:
  - an empty or whitespace-only COLUMN value gives `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`;

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
error. At least one KEY is needed.

## filter

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
table with no row left still prints its header.

## group

`tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
`mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
`2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
usage error.

## join

`tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
`max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

README list, so expect to touch the same lines as the others. Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them:
do not add a second way to do something it already does.

## Problem Statement

`tabula` (Python 3.9+, standard library only) has four commands (`show`, `head`, `cols`, `apply`) in `tabula/engine.py`. The user wants seven more table commands — `sort`, `filter`, `group`, `join`, `pivot`, `dedupe`, `stats` — plus two new options, `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`. Everything that works today has to keep working: the four commands, their output, their exit statuses, `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command, and `import tabula`.

## Solution

Each command is a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function in `tabula/engine.py` that returns a `Table`, with one entry in `COMMANDS`. Each also gets its own test file `tests/test_NAME.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats, after the four existing sections and written like them) and a line in the README command list.

Before anything is added, the conventions the module already has become one shared helper each (see Implementation Decisions). Every new command uses those helpers. None of them adds a second way to do the same thing.

## User Stories

1. As a CSV user, I can `tabula sort FILE KEY...` with `:num`/`:desc` modifiers and get a stable multi-key sort.
2. As a CSV user, I can `tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` with `== != >= <= > < ~` and get only the rows where every condition holds.
3. As a CSV user, I can `tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`.
4. As a CSV user, I can `tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` with `--kind inner|left`.
5. As a CSV user, I can `tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` to sum VALUE into a cross table.
6. As a CSV user, I can `tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` with `--keep first|last`.
7. As a CSV user, I can `tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` to get count/min/max/mean/median for each column.
8. As a user of the four existing commands, I see no change in their output or exit statuses.

## Implementation Decisions

General rules, from the brief, for every command:
- `--format text|csv|json` (text by default) prints the result table.
- A mistake in a file or in the request prints `tabula: <message>` on stderr, nothing on stdout, and exits 1 (`TabulaError`).
- A command line that is not shaped right exits 2 (`UsageError`): a missing or extra argument, an unknown option, a bad option value, a condition with no operator.
- A column named in a request that the file lacks exits 1, and the message names the column (reuse `Table.index`).
- "row N" counts the file's data rows from 1, header not counted, in file order (never sorted order).
- A **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts. All arithmetic is `Decimal`, never float.
- **Shape checks come before the file is read.** Usage errors (exit 2) are raised before `load`, as `head` does today. Column-existence and cell mistakes (exit 1) come after.

### Shared groundwork: done in issue 1 (`sort`), reused by the other six

"Finish the module's own conventions before adding to them: do not add a second way to do something it already does."
1. **Option reading.** Replace the hard-coded `--format` branch in `parse_args` with one table of choice options, e.g. `OPTIONS = {"format": (FORMATS, "text"), "kind": (("inner", "left"), "inner"), "keep": (("first", "last"), "first")}`, read by one loop that handles both `--opt value` and `--opt=value`. Defaults go into `opts`, so `opts["kind"]` and `opts["keep"]` always exist. Any command line accepts all three options, before or after the command. A bad value is a UsageError, as `--format` is today. The existing `--format` messages stay word for word (`--format needs a value`, `--format must be one of text, csv, json, got 'x'`). Update the usage line in `usage_text()` and the intro of `docs/commands.md` to mention `--kind` and `--keep`.
2. **Argument counts.** Extend `_need_args` so it can also check "at least N" (e.g. `_need_args(args, 2, "sort FILE KEY...", at_least=True)`), and make `cmd_apply` use it, with an unchanged message. Every new command checks its count with `_need_args`.
3. **Row/cell errors.** `cmd_apply` already wraps a cell mistake as `"%s: row %d: %s"`. Make that one helper. On top of it, add a cell-number helper built on `_need_number`/`to_decimal` that raises exactly `FILE: row N: column 'C': 'abc' is not a number`; `%r` is used for both the column and the value, as `_need_number` does. `sort :num`, `group`, `pivot` and `stats` all use this helper. `apply`'s output is unchanged.
4. **Number printing.** Plain numbers (sum/min/max/pivot cells) use the existing `fmt_decimal`, which gives no exponent, no `+` and no negative zero, and keeps `10.50` as `10.50`. Add one helper for "rounded half up to two decimals, always two" (`Decimal("0.01")`, `ROUND_HALF_UP`, then `fmt_decimal`). `group mean`, `stats mean` and `stats median` all use it. A negative zero such as `-0.001` prints `0.00`.
5. **Value comparison.** Add one helper for "compare as numbers when both are numbers, else as text by code point", used by `filter`. `sort :num` uses the cell-number helper; plain `sort` compares text.
6. **Tests.** Move the `run_cli` helper from `tests/test_engine.py` into a shared test-support module (e.g. `tests/support.py`). `test_engine.py` and every new `tests/test_NAME.py` import it from there. Do not copy it.
7. **README.** Turn the README's inline "Commands today: …" sentence into a bulleted command list, one line per command (the four existing ones first). Each command issue then adds its own line in the order sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats.

### Per-command decisions (brief text plus the gaps the brief left open)

**sort** `sort FILE KEY...` (at least one KEY; usage `sort FILE KEY...`)
- A KEY is split on `:`. The first part is the column; each further part must be `num` or `desc`, in either order. A modifier given twice, an unknown modifier, or an empty column part is a usage error.
- Text compares by code point (`B` < `a`). `:num` compares Decimals, and a non-number cell (an empty one included) gives the cell-number error. `:desc` puts the largest first.
- The sort is stable on every key: rows tied on all keys keep file order, also with `:desc`. Use successive stable `sorted` passes from the last key to the first, with `reverse=` for desc. Python's `reverse=True` keeps stability.

**filter** `filter FILE CONDITION...` (at least one)
- Operators: `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`. The operator is the one that starts earliest in the argument; where two start at the same place, the longer one wins. The column is the text before it and VALUE the text after it (VALUE may be empty).
- No operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. An unknown column is exit 1.
- For every operator but `~`: if the cell and VALUE are both numbers (`to_decimal`), they are compared as Decimals (`10` > `9`, `1.0` == `1`); otherwise as text by code point.
- `~`: VALUE is contained in the cell, ignoring case, via `.lower()` on both, as `t_icontains` does.
- Rows stay in file order. With no rows left, the header still prints.

**group** `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` (at least one AGGREGATE)
- An AGGREGATE is `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C` or `mean:C`. Anything else (including `count:x`, `sum:` and an unknown name) is a usage error, and so is the same aggregate twice.
- The output columns are BY, then one per aggregate named with `:` replaced by `_`. If that gives the same column name twice (e.g. BY is `count`), it is a mistake (exit 1) naming the column.
- One row per distinct BY value, in order of first appearance. `count` is the number of rows in the group.
- sum/min/max print with `fmt_decimal` (min/max print the Decimal of the winning cell; among equal values, the first in file order wins). `mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, printed with the 2-decimal helper. Any non-number cell (an empty one included) in an aggregated column gives the cell-number error.

**join** `join LEFT RIGHT KEY` (exactly three)
- KEY must be in both files (exit 1 otherwise, naming the file and the column).
- The result columns are the LEFT columns, then the RIGHT columns except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` appended. If that still leaves a duplicate name, it is a mistake (exit 1).
- A match is exact text equality. `--kind inner` (the default) gives, for each LEFT row in order, one row per matching RIGHT row in RIGHT order. `--kind left` also gives an unmatched LEFT row once, with `""` in the RIGHT columns.

**pivot** `pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` (exactly four)
- ROW == COLUMN is a usage error. VALUE may be the same column as ROW or COLUMN.
- The result columns are ROW, then each distinct COLUMN value in order of first appearance. There is one row per distinct ROW value in order of first appearance.
- A cell is the exact sum of VALUE (printed with `fmt_decimal`); a pair that never occurs is `0`.
- Mistakes are checked row by row in file order:
  - an empty or whitespace-only COLUMN value gives `FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`;
  - a COLUMN value equal to the ROW column's name is a mistake naming the row and the duplicate column;
  - a non-number VALUE gives the cell-number error.

**dedupe** `dedupe FILE KEY...` (at least one)
- Rows with equal text in all the KEY columns form a set. `--keep first` (the default) keeps the first row of each set and `--keep last` keeps the last. The kept rows stay in file order. Repeating a KEY is harmless.

**stats** `stats FILE COLUMN...` (at least one)
- One row per COLUMN, in the order asked (repeats allowed), with the columns `column,count,min,max,mean,median`.
- Only non-empty cells count (`cell.strip() != ""`), and each of them must be a number (cell-number error otherwise).
- min/max print with `fmt_decimal`; mean and median use the 2-decimal helper. The median of an even count is the exact mean of the two middle values.
- A column with no numbers at all gives `COLUMN,0,,,,`.

## Testing Decisions

- Each command has `tests/test_NAME.py` (unittest), driven through the CLI with the shared `run_cli` from the test-support module. Assert the exit status, the exact stdout and the stderr (empty on success; `tabula: …` and empty stdout on failure), across text/csv/json where it matters.
- Cover every rule above: each exit-2 shape error, each exit-1 mistake with its exact message, ordering and stability, Decimal exactness (e.g. `0.1+0.2` sums to `0.3`), rounding (`2.25`, `5.00`, half-up `0.125` → `0.13`), and the `--opt value` and `--opt=value` forms placed before and after the command.
- Issue 1 also tests the shared option reading (all three options accepted on old commands, bad values exit 2) and checks that `tests/test_engine.py` still passes unchanged in behaviour.
- The full suite `python3 -m unittest discover tests` must pass after every merge.

## Out of Scope

- New dependencies, non-CSV input, changes to transforms or to the existing four commands' behaviour, and float arithmetic.
- Options other than `--kind` and `--keep`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_args` reads `--format`, `--kind`, `--keep` from one option table; `--kind`/`--keep` are accepted on any command line, before or after the command, as `--opt v` or `--opt=v`; a bad value exits 2; `--format` messages are unchanged
- [ ] One "at least N arguments" check (`_need_args`), one row-error helper, one cell-number helper (`FILE: row N: column 'C': 'x' is not a number`), one 2-decimal formatter; `apply` uses the shared helpers with unchanged output
- [ ] `run_cli` lives in one shared test-support module, used by `test_engine.py` and every new test file
- [ ] `sort`: multi-key, `:num`/`:desc` in either order, code-point text order, stable (also with `:desc`); a duplicate or unknown modifier and no KEY exit 2; a non-number with `:num` exits 1 with the exact message
- [ ] `filter`: all seven operators; earliest operator wins and the longest wins at the same place; numeric comparison when both sides are numbers; `~` case-insensitive; no operator, empty column and no condition exit 2; no rows still prints the header
- [ ] `group`: first-appearance order; `count/sum/min/max/mean` columns named `X_C`; plain-number printing; mean to 2dp half up; a bad or duplicate aggregate and no aggregate exit 2; a non-number exits 1; a duplicate output column exits 1
- [ ] `join`: LEFT columns then RIGHT minus KEY; `_right` renaming; a remaining duplicate exits 1; inner/left semantics and ordering; not exactly 3 args exits 2
- [ ] `pivot`: column/row order by first appearance; exact sums; missing pairs are `0`; ROW==COLUMN exits 2; an empty COLUMN value, a COLUMN value equal to the ROW name and a non-number VALUE exit 1; not exactly 4 args exits 2
- [ ] `dedupe`: `--keep first|last`; kept rows in file order; no KEY exits 2
- [ ] `stats`: `column,count,min,max,mean,median`; blank cells skipped; exact median; 2dp mean/median; `COLUMN,0,,,,` when there are no numbers; no COLUMN exits 2
- [ ] Each command has a `COMMANDS` entry, `tests/test_NAME.py`, a `docs/commands.md` section (order: sort, filter, group, join, pivot, dedupe, stats) and a README list line
- [ ] The four existing commands, their output and exit statuses, `pip install .` → `tabula`, and `import tabula` still work; the full test suite passes

## Original request

# Tabula: seven more commands

This repository already holds **tabula**, a small Python tool I use on CSV files (Python 3.9 or newer, standard
library only). Read the code first: `README.md`, `tabula/engine.py` and `tests/`. It has four commands today (`show`,
`head`, `cols`, `apply`), reads CSV files, and prints a table as text, CSV or JSON. I want seven more commands. They
all go into the same module, `tabula/engine.py`, the way the first four did: a `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` function that
returns a `Table`, one entry in `COMMANDS`. Keep what is there working: the four commands, their output, their exit
statuses, and `pip install .` giving the `tabula` command and `import tabula`. Each command also gets its own test file `tests/test_COMMAND.py`, a section in `docs/commands.md` (one section per
command, in the order of the sections below, written like the four that are there) and a line in the command list of `README.md`.

How a command behaves in general is already settled by the code and stays as it is: `--format text|csv|json` (text by
default) says how the result table is printed; a mistake in a file or in what I asked for prints
`tabula: <message>` on standard error and exits 1, with nothing on standard output; a command line that is not shaped
right (a missing argument, an unknown option, a condition with no operator) exits 2. A "row N" in a message counts the
data rows of the file from 1, the header not counted, in the order of the file (not the sorted order). Cell values are
text; a **number** is what `to_decimal` accepts (an optional sign, digits, an optional decimal point; no exponent, no
thousands marks). All arithmetic is exact (`Decimal`), never floating point. A column named in a request that the file
does not have is a mistake in the request (exit 1, the message names the column).

Two options are new and are read by one command each, but they are accepted on any command line, before or after the
command: `--kind inner|left` and `--keep first|last`, each as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`. Any other value is a
usage error (exit 2).

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A KEY is a column
name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest first), in
either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The sort is
stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not a
number is a mistake: `FILE: row N: column 'price': 'abc' is not a number`. A modifier given twice in one KEY is a usage
error. At least one KEY is needed.

## filter

`tabula filter FILE CONDITION...` prints the rows where every CONDITION holds, in the order of the file. A CONDITION
is one argument shaped `COLUMN OP VALUE` with no spaces added: `price>=10`, `city==Leeds`, `name~gnome`. The operators
are `==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<` and `~` (the cell contains VALUE, ignoring upper and lower case). The operator is
the first one that appears in the argument (so a column name cannot contain one of them), and where two start at the
same place the longer one (`>=` and not `>`). For every operator but `~`, when both the cell and VALUE are numbers
they are compared as numbers (`10` is greater than `9`, `1.0` equals `1`); otherwise as text, by code point. An
argument with no operator, or nothing before the operator, is a usage error. At least one CONDITION is needed. A
table with no row left still prints its header.

## group

`tabula group FILE BY AGGREGATE...` prints one row per distinct value of column BY, in the order each value first
appears, with the columns BY and then one per AGGREGATE, named as written with `:` replaced by `_` (`sum_qty`). An
AGGREGATE is `count` (rows in the group) or `sum:COLUMN`, `min:COLUMN`, `max:COLUMN`, `mean:COLUMN` over the numbers of
that column. `sum`, `min` and `max` are printed as plain numbers (no `+` sign, no exponent; `10.50` stays `10.50`).
`mean` is the exact sum divided by the count, rounded half up to two decimals and always printed with two (`5.00`,
`2.25`). A cell that is not a number in a column being summed, compared or averaged is a mistake (the same
message as in `sort`). At least one AGGREGATE is needed; one that is not one of those, or the same one twice, is a
usage error.

## join

`tabula join LEFT RIGHT KEY` joins two files on the column KEY, which both must have. The result has the columns of
LEFT, then the columns of RIGHT except KEY. A RIGHT column whose name LEFT already has gets `_right` added to its name.
If that still leaves two columns of the same name the result cannot be printed: that is a mistake. Values match when
the text is exactly equal. With `--kind inner` (the default) the rows are, for each LEFT row in the order of LEFT, one
row per matching RIGHT row in the order of RIGHT; a LEFT row with no match is left out. With `--kind left` a LEFT row
with no match appears once, with empty text in the RIGHT columns. Exactly three arguments are needed.

## pivot

`tabula pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE` turns the distinct values of column COLUMN into columns. The result has the column
ROW, then one column per distinct value of COLUMN in the order each first appears; one row per distinct value of ROW in
the order each first appears. A cell is the exact sum of the numbers in VALUE for the rows with that ROW and that
COLUMN value, printed as in `group`; a pair that never occurs is `0`. ROW and COLUMN must be different columns (usage
error otherwise). An empty value in COLUMN is a mistake (`FILE: row N: column 'C': empty value`), and so is a value of
COLUMN equal to the name of the ROW column, because the result would have a column name twice. A non-number in VALUE is
a mistake as in `sort`. Exactly four arguments are needed.

## dedupe

`tabula dedupe FILE KEY...` drops rows whose values in all the KEY columns equal those of another row (text equality).
With `--keep first` (the default) the first row of each such set stays; with `--keep last` the last one stays. The
rows that stay keep the relative order they have in the file. At least one KEY is needed.

## stats

`tabula stats FILE COLUMN...` prints one row per COLUMN, in the order asked, with the columns `column`, `count`, `min`,
`max`, `mean`, `median`. The statistics are over the cells of that column that are not empty (a cell of only
whitespace counts as empty); all of those must be numbers (mistake as in `sort` otherwise). `count` is how many there
are. `min` and `max` print as in `group`; `mean` and `median` are rounded half up to two decimals and always printed
with two (the median of an even count is the mean of the two middle numbers, taken exactly). With no numbers at all the
row is `COLUMN`, `0` and four empty cells. At least one COLUMN is needed.

# tabula

Small tools for CSV tables, standard library only (Python 3.9 or newer).

    tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...

Commands (`docs/commands.md` describes them, `docs/transforms.md` the transforms):

- `show FILE`: print a table
- `head FILE N`: the first N rows
- `cols FILE`: the column names, numbered
- `apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...`: run transforms over one column
- `sort FILE KEY...`: sort rows by one or more keys (`:num`, `:desc`)
- `filter FILE CONDITION...`: keep the rows that meet every condition (`==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`)
- `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...`: one row per BY value, with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`
- `join LEFT RIGHT KEY`: join two files on a key column (`--kind inner|left`)
- `pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE`: one row per ROW value, one column per COLUMN value, cells are the sum of VALUE
- `dedupe FILE KEY...`: one row per set of equal KEY values, the first or the last (`--keep first|last`)
- `stats FILE COLUMN...`: count, min, max, mean and median of the numbers in each COLUMN

Everything lives in `tabula/engine.py`: the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the commands.
A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table`, registered in `COMMANDS`.
Mistakes in a file or a request exit 1 with `tabula: <message>` on stderr; a badly shaped command line exits 2.
Run the tests with `python -m unittest discover tests`.
"""Shared test support: run the tabula command line in a scratch directory holding the given files."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..")


def run_cli(*argv, files=None):
    """(exit status, stdout, stderr) of `python -m tabula ARGV` run in a temp dir that holds `files` {name: text}."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        for k, v in (files or {}).items():
            with open(os.path.join(d, k), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as fh:
                fh.write(v)
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'tabula'] + list(argv), cwd=d, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

## sort

`tabula sort FILE KEY...` prints the whole table with its rows sorted by the first KEY, ties by the second, and so on. A
KEY is a column name, optionally followed by the modifiers `:num` (compare as numbers, not as text) and `:desc` (largest
first), in either order (`price:num:desc`, `price:desc:num`). Text compares by code point (so `B` sorts before `a`). The
sort is stable: rows that tie on every key keep the order of the file, also with `:desc`. With `:num`, a cell that is not
a number (an empty one too) is a mistake that names the file, the row and the column (`t.csv: row 2: column 'price':
'abc' is not a number`). A modifier given twice in one KEY, an unknown modifier, an empty column name, or no KEY at all
is a usage error.

# Commands

`tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...` reads CSV files (UTF-8, an
optional byte order mark, LF or CRLF) and prints a table. Every command returns a `Table`; `--format` says how it is
printed (text by default). `--kind` (default `inner`) and `--keep` (default `first`) are each read by one command, but
every command line accepts them, before or after the command, as `--opt value` or `--opt=value`; any other value is a
usage error. A mistake in a file or in a request exits 1 with `tabula: <message>` on standard error; a command line that
is not shaped right exits 2.

## show

`tabula show FILE` prints the whole table. Blank lines in the file are ignored. A row with more or fewer fields than the
header is a mistake that names the file and the line (`t.csv: line 3: expected 2 fields, found 1`).

## head

`tabula head FILE N` prints the header and the first N rows. N is a whole number (zero is fine); anything else is a usage
error.

## cols

`tabula cols FILE` prints one row per column with two columns, `position` (from 1) and `column`.

`tabula apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...` runs each TRANSFORM, left to right, over every value of one column and prints the

# tabula

Small tools for CSV tables, standard library only (Python 3.9 or newer).

    tabula [--format text|csv|json] [--kind inner|left] [--keep first|last] COMMAND ARGS...

Commands (`docs/commands.md` describes them, `docs/transforms.md` the transforms):

- `show FILE`: print a table
- `head FILE N`: the first N rows
- `cols FILE`: the column names, numbered
- `apply FILE COLUMN TRANSFORM...`: run transforms over one column
- `sort FILE KEY...`: sort rows by one or more keys (`:num`, `:desc`)
- `filter FILE CONDITION...`: keep the rows that meet every condition (`==`, `!=`, `>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `~`)
- `group FILE BY AGGREGATE...`: one row per BY value, with `count`, `sum:C`, `min:C`, `max:C`, `mean:C`
- `join LEFT RIGHT KEY`: join two files on a key column (`--kind inner|left`)
- `pivot FILE ROW COLUMN VALUE`: one row per ROW value, one column per COLUMN value, cells are the sum of VALUE
- `dedupe FILE KEY...`: one row per set of equal KEY values, the first or the last (`--keep first|last`)
- `stats FILE COLUMN...`: count, min, max, mean and median of the numbers in each COLUMN

Everything lives in `tabula/engine.py`: the table model, the transforms, the output formats and the commands.
A command is a function `cmd_NAME(args, opts)` returning a `Table`, registered in `COMMANDS`.
Mistakes in a file or a request exit 1 with `tabula: <message>` on stderr; a badly shaped command line exits 2.
Run the tests with `python -m unittest discover tests`.
"""Shared test support: run the tabula command line in a scratch directory holding the given files."""
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile

ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..")


def run_cli(*argv, files=None):
    """(exit status, stdout, stderr) of `python -m tabula ARGV` run in a temp dir that holds `files` {name: text}."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        for k, v in (files or {}).items():
            with open(os.path.join(d, k), 'w', encoding='utf-8', newline='') as fh:
                fh.write(v)
        env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=ROOT)
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-m', 'tabula'] + list(argv), cwd=d, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

content.text:
PRD #1 is signed off: I added the `reviewed` label and posted the sign-off comment. All acceptance criteria are met. I filed one follow-up issue, #17, and left closing the PRD to the engine, which will do it once #17 is closed.

- **Test suite:** all 172 tests pass. I recorded the commit they ran against on PRD #1 so the release step can reuse the result.
- **Brief checks:** I ran one command per rule in the original brief for all seven commands and the new `--kind` / `--keep` options. All behaved as written: ordering, stable sort, operator choice in `filter`, exact `Decimal` sums, rounding to two decimals (negatives too), every error message and exit status. `pip install .` still gives the `tabula` command, and `import tabula` works.
- **Robustness checks:**
  - 5000-digit numbers stay exact through every calculation.
  - A byte order mark, CRLF and lone-CR line endings, a form feed, and U+2028 inside a field are all handled.
  - Invalid UTF-8 gives `tabula: … not valid UTF-8` and exits 1.
  - Output piped into `head -1` exits 0 quietly.
- **One defect, filed as #17:** if output can't be written (`> /dev/full`), tabula crashes with a Python traceback and exits 120. It should print `tabula: <message>` and exit 1. The original four commands already did this, so it isn't new, but every command shows it. The review rules count any traceback as a blocking defect, so I filed it.
- **Not filed:** an argument starting with a dash (e.g. `-x`) is rejected as an unknown option, exit 2. That is how the original argument parsing worked, and the brief says it stays as it is.

The security audit is turned off for this run, and the PRD has no Quality bar, so neither of those steps ran. I opened no PRs.
